body_markdown:
*SDPA analysis demonstrates DecisionDx-Melanoma can identify higher-risk patients within a traditionally low-risk population with thin melanomas*


*Dermato-Onco2026 analysis supports the test's ability to provide individualized five-year recurrence-risk estimates in stage I–III melanoma*


FRIENDSWOOD, Texas


, Nov. 11, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Castle Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: CSTL), a company improving health through innovative tests that guide patient care, today announced it will present new data on DecisionDx-Melanoma at the Society of Dermatology Physician Associates (SDPA) 24th Annual Fall Dermatology Conference, taking place Nov. 11-15, 2026, in Hollywood, Florida, and the 3rd European Congress on Dermato-Oncology (Dermato-Onco2026), taking place Nov. 12-13, 2026, in Rotterdam, The Netherlands.


More precise assessment of a patient's risk of melanoma recurrence or death can help clinicians tailor follow-up and surveillance to each patient's individual needs. The analyses being presented evaluate DecisionDx-Melanoma, Castle's CP+GEP test that combines an independently validated 31-gene expression profile (GEP) score with clinicopathologic (CP) factors. The studies assess the test's ability to identify patients with thin T1a tumors at elevated risk of melanoma-specific mortality and the performance of its i31-ROR algorithm, which is designed to provide individualized five-year recurrence-risk estimates. Together, the data reinforce the value of combining tumor biology with CP factors to refine risk assessment beyond American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging and inform more personalized, risk-aligned patient care.


"A thin melanoma may be reassuring, but these findings remind us that some of those patients still face a higher risk of dying from their disease," said study author Harrison Nguyen, M.D., MBA, MPH, board-certified dermatologist at Harrison Dermatology and Research Group in Missouri City, Texas. "The additional prognostic information provided by DecisionDx-Melanoma can help us explain to patients why we may recommend closer follow-up, even when their tumor's traditional features appear favorable."


**SDPA: Identifying Higher-Risk Patients with Thin Melanomas**


Castle's data at SDPA will be shared in a digital poster, which may be viewed directly through the official conference app **.**


**ePoster Title:** The 31-gene expression profile test identifies patients with AJCC T1a (<0.8 mm) cutaneous melanoma at increased risk of 5-year melanoma-specific mortality


- First author: Harrison Nguyen, M.D., MBA, MPH, FAAD


**Summary:** This study evaluated 750 patients with thin T1a cutaneous melanomas (<0.8 mm), a tumor category traditionally considered low risk under AJCC staging, who were diagnosed between 2013 to 2019 and had at least five years of follow-up or died from their disease. The study linked DecisionDx-Melanoma results from patients tested in clinical care with survival outcomes recorded in the National Cancer Institute's Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program registries. The analysis demonstrated that DecisionDx-Melanoma:


- **Identified higher-risk patients in approximately 1 in 8 cases:** Nearly 12% of patients with T1a tumors (88 of 750) received a Class 1B/2A (increased-risk, n=59) or Class 2B (highest-risk, n=29) result, identifying a subset of patients with elevated melanoma-specific mortality risk despite having thin primary tumors.
- **Significantly stratified five-year melanoma-specific survival (MSS)** : Survival was 97.1% for patients with Class 1A (lowest-risk) results, compared with 88.1% for patients with Class 1B/2A (increased-risk) results and 86.2% for patients with Class 2B (highest-risk) results (p<0.001). Patients with higher-risk classes had similar survival rates to patients with T2b tumors (82.4%) or stage IIA melanoma (85.1%).


These findings demonstrate that patients with thin T1a melanomas can have different biological risk profiles and outcomes. DecisionDx-Melanoma can help identify those at elevated risk who may benefit from increased surveillance or more proactive management, providing additional insight into each patient's prognosis to guide more individualized, risk-aligned care.


At SDPA, Castle will also present an ePoster titled "Clinical Utility of the 487-Gene Expression Profile Test for Atopic Dermatitis in a Private Practice Setting," featuring a case series with outcome data evaluating the use of AdvanceAD-Tx™ in 17 patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD).


**Dermato-Onco2026: Individualized Five-Year Recurrence-Risk Assessment**


Castle's data at Dermato-Onco2026 will be shared in an oral presentation as well as a digital poster, which may be viewed in the E-Poster Gallery during the conference.


**Abstract Title:** The i31-ROR stratifies patients with cutaneous melanoma by high and low 5-year recurrence risk to better inform management decisions


- **Abstract Number:** 137
- **Session #9:** Short Presentations Young Investigators
- **Date and Time:** Friday, Nov. 13, 1:50–2:00 p.m. Central European Time


**Summary:** This study evaluated 1,726 patients with stage I–III cutaneous melanoma from 49 U.S. sites, representing one of Castle's largest retrospective melanoma cohorts. All patients underwent DecisionDx-Melanoma testing between 2013 and 2018 as part of their clinical care, providing a large, real-world dataset to evaluate the test's ability to predict patient outcomes.


The study focused on i31-ROR, one of DecisionDx-Melanoma's integrated algorithms, which is designed to combine the test's GEP class score with CP factors to provide an individualized five-year recurrence-risk estimate. This study suggests that DecisionDx-Melanoma can give clinicians a patient-specific risk estimate beyond the population-based risk associated with a broad staging category, helping inform how closely an individual patient should be followed.


The study demonstrated that DecisionDx-Melanoma's i31-ROR algorithm:


- **Predicted five-year recurrence more accurately than AJCC staging:** The i31-ROR better distinguished patients who experienced recurrence within five years from those who did not, supporting the value of individualized recurrence-risk assessment.
- **Distinguished patients with low and high recurrence risk:** Five-year recurrence-free survival was 92.5% among patients with low-risk i31-ROR results versus 54.2% among those with high-risk results (p<0.001).
- **Identified significant differences in distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and MSS:** Patients with low-risk i31-ROR results had five-year DMFS of 94.7%, compared with 68.3% for those with high-risk results (p<0.001). Five-year MSS was 98.4% for patients with low-risk results versus 81.6% for those with high-risk results (p<0.001).


These findings support the use of DecisionDx-Melanoma's individualized five-year recurrence-risk estimates to guide risk-aligned clinical decisions, including patient follow-up and surveillance.


**About DecisionDx-Melanoma**
DecisionDx-Melanoma is a gene expression profile (GEP) test designed to analyze tumor biology to deliver a personalized risk assessment for patients with stage I–III cutaneous melanoma, enhancing risk stratification beyond American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging alone. By combining molecular insights with select clinicopathologic features, the test provides two distinct outputs: a personalized risk of sentinel lymph node (SLN) positivity and a personalized risk of recurrence and/or metastasis. This clinically actionable information is designed to help guide risk-aligned patient management decisions, including SLN biopsy consideration, follow-up intensity, imaging, and referrals.


DecisionDx-Melanoma is supported by 58 peer-reviewed publications, including prospective studies and meta-analyses, and was developed in collaboration with more than 100 leading U.S. institutions. The test has been clinically validated in more than 10,000 patient samples, ordered more than 260,000 times since launch, and has been shown to be associated with improved patient survival. Learn more at[www.CastleBiosciences.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4819754-1&h=574011310&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.castlebiosciences.com%2F&a=www.CastleBiosciences.com) .


**About AdvanceAD-Tx** AdvanceAD-Tx is a non-invasive gene expression profile (GEP) test designed to guide systemic treatment decisions for patients aged 12 years and older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD). Using RNA expression data from lesional skin scraping samples—no biopsy required—the test evaluates 487 genes across 12 inflammatory and cutaneous biology pathways to reveal the underlying immune biology driving an individual patient's disease. The test classifies patients into one of two molecular profiles: a Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitor Responder Profile or a T helper type 2 (Th2) Molecular Profile.


The prospective, clinical validation study showed that the test identifies a subset of patients with a JAK Inhibitor Responder Profile who experience significantly greater clinical benefit—including improved and faster skin clearance (EASI-90), reduced itch, fewer flares and better quality of life by three months— when treated with a JAK inhibitor therapy compared to those treated with a Th2-targeted therapy. AdvanceAD-Tx provides clinicians with objective, molecular-based insights to help personalize systemic treatment decisions and improve care for patients. Learn more at[https://castlebiosciences.com/tests/therapy-guidance/advancead-tx/overview](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4819754-1&h=1311539046&u=https%3A%2F%2Fcastlebiosciences.com%2Ftests%2Ftherapy-guidance%2Fadvancead-tx%2Foverview&a=https%3A%2F%2Fcastlebiosciences.com%2Ftests%2Ftherapy-guidance%2Fadvancead-tx%2Foverview) .
